Where it began

Karun Nair was born in Jodhpur, Rajasthan, on 6 December 1991, into a family with roots in Kerala. They later settled in Koramangala, Bangalore, and on 28 March 2001 he joined the Koramangala Cricket Academy, where his coach was Shivanand. He moved to the Frank Anthony Public School because it offered more cricket, and later studied commerce at Jain University.

He speaks five languages: English, Hindi, Malayalam, Kannada and Tamil. Few dressing rooms can have left him lost for words.

Runs for Karnataka

He arrived in first-class cricket in 2013–14, the season Karnataka won the Ranji Trophy, and celebrated with hundreds in three matches in a row. The next season began quietly, but he saved his best for the final, making 328 as Karnataka took the title again. At the time no one had made more in a Ranji final, and no one had made a triple hundred in one since 1946–47.

His appetite never faded. In January 2025, in the Vijay Hazare Trophy, he made 542 runs before anyone got him out, setting a new world record in List A cricket, with three hundreds in a row across five unbeaten innings.

Three hundred and three

His Test debut came against England at Mohali on 26 November 2016. In only his third Test innings, at Chennai, he went to his first hundred and kept going until he had 303 not out. Only Virender Sehwag had made a Test triple century for India before him, and only two men in the whole history of the game had turned a first Test hundred into three hundred. India won by an innings and 75 runs, and he was player of the match.

After that, Test chances were hard to come by. He had a long wait before a double hundred for India A against the England Lions earned him a recall in May 2025, and he batted at number three in that summer's Anderson-Tendulkar Trophy. In 10 Tests between 2016 and 2025 he made 579 runs at 41.36 and held 10 catches.

In the IPL and beyond

He played in the IPL for Royal Challengers Bangalore, Rajasthan Royals, Delhi, Kings XI Punjab and Kolkata Knight Riders. His breakthrough came with Rajasthan in 2014, when he made 330 runs at a strike rate of 142.24, and he captained Delhi in three matches in 2017. Back with the Delhi Capitals in 2025, he marked his return with 89 from 40 balls against Mumbai Indians. In 2023 he even turned out for a club side in the West of England Premier League.

And finally

He sent down some off-breaks in Tests too, without ever troubling the wicket column. He can hardly have minded. More than half of all his Test runs came in a single innings, and it is hard to think of a better one to have.
